timeline.body:
- Vendor registry files needed for Bazel module resolution to achieve
offline build with vendor mode.
- Also refactored bazel_vendor_test to avoid vendoring dependencies of
  bazel_tools, which speeds up the test significantly.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/22554

timeline.body: Could we make this a field instead of `vendorDir`?

reply.body: Totally, thanks for the suggestion!

timeline.body:
This could probably be parallelized across all repos. 

Do we need to worry about atomicity, e.g. if users interrupt the vendor command? Maybe we should atomically move the marker files into their final location at the end?

reply.body:
Indeed, I left a TODO for parallelizing. 

But I think copying one marker file after vendoring one repo source is fine? If the vendoring is interrupted, the user probably doesn't want to re-vendor what's already been vendored?

If the copying of the marker file was atomic then I would agree, but what if the marker file is only written partially and then happens to become identical to an up-to-date one even if the contents aren't?
I see! Updated the code to copy the marker file to a tmp file first and then rename it.
there's technically still potential for races unless we actually have a proper locking scheme (eg. multiple Bazels can be working in the same workspace). but we can leave that for future PRs.

> multiple Bazels can be working in the same workspace

Do you mean when they have different output base? That's general not a recommended use case, right?

I just noticed I didn't clean up the old vendor directory, so also updated here.

Another idea I have: how about we just move the repo from external to vendor dir and leave a symlink behind? That would say a lot of copying time. But may have problem with symlink, but the current copying action also doesn't deal with symlink well.
Yeah moving + leaving a symlink sounds good to me. In fact I think that was my expectation in the beginning, before we settled on copying (can't remember why now).

Symlinking does make a small semantic difference: If `external/A` is vendored and thus symlinked to `~/workspace/vendor/A`, but `external/B` is not, then `external/A/../B` will point to `~/workspace/vendor/B`, which doesn't exist. This may turn out fine, but it may also end up breaking some repo rules.

> then external/A/../B will point to ~/workspace/vendor/B

This only happens when the symlink is resolved somehow, right? Do people actually use this pattern to locate another repo? I would consider this is a hack?

I have used something like this in the past to point `--repo_env=JAVA_HOME` to the embedded JDK for r_j_e's coursier and I could see some repo rules doing this, but I do agree it's a hack :-) I just wanted to point out that we should have such breakages on our radar when we make this optimization (I think we still should).

> Yeah moving + leaving a symlink sounds good to me. 

I ended up not doing this. It could cause problem in this situation:
1. vendor a repo foo: now external/foo -> vendor_dir/foo
2. Remove --vendor_dir
3. Think vendor mode is off, and I can change vendor_dir/foo freely (e.g. delete it)
4. Build breaks because external/foo still points to the modified source

timeline.body: Could this take in a `RepositoryName`? Then we clearly wouldn't have to worry about slashes in `repoName`.

reply.body: SG, also extracted the marker file name to a function in `RepositoryName`

timeline.body: Does this also clean up unused registry files?

reply.body: Nope, we also don't clean up unused vendored repo yet. I'm not sure we should do that by default, what if the user actually wants to switch between registries in a offline mode. We can probably implement a tidy mode later to clean up unused vendored content.
Sounds good!

timeline.body: doesn't this change mean clearing `--vendor_dir` has no effect for a subsequent command?

reply.body: Ah, nice catch! Refactored the code along with the `getVendorPath` change.

timeline.body: this seems to duplicate the logic in BazelRepositoryModule. can we somehow unify the two?

reply.body: Thanks! Turned out we can just do `workspace.getRelative()`, it deals with absolute path already. This also helped me discover a nullpointerexception bug in BazelRepositoryModule!

timeline.body:
1. maybe remove 'cache' as the vendor dir isn't really a cache? 
2. this name could collide with a repo name. maybe call it '_registry' as normally repo names can't start with an underscore?

reply.body: Done, also extracted it to a constant string.

timeline.body: I think this class has a clear enough identity that we don't need to call it `VendorUtil`. It seems to be managing the entire contents of the vendor directory. So we could actually just name it `VendorDirectoryManager`, or `VendorManager`, or `VendorDirectory`... all just suggestions!

reply.body: I'll pick `VendorManager`, thanks for the advice!

timeline.message:
Vendor registry files

- Vendor registry files needed for Bazel module resolution to achieve
offline build with vendor mode.
- Also refactored bazel_vendor_test to avoid vendoring dependencies of
  bazel_tools, which speeds up the test significantly.

Fixes https://github.com/bazelbuild/bazel/issues/22554
timeline.author: Yun Peng

+### Build the target offline {:#build-the-target-offline}
+
+With the external dependencies vendored, you can build the target offline by
+
+```none
+bazel build --vendor_dir=vendor_src //src/main:hello-world //src/test/...
+```
+
+The build should work in a clean build environment without network access and repository cache.
+
+Therefore, you should be able to check in the vendored source and build the same targets offline on another machine.
+
+Note: If you build different targets or change the external dependencies, build configuration, or Bazel version, you may need to re-vendor.
+

Hello,
If I understand this change correctly, it would also be super useful for building Bazel itself in an air gapped environment (like the nix sandbox).
Is there any chance that this PR can be backported to the 7.x stream?
It would greatly simplify the packaging of Bazel (and potentially other projects using Bazel) in nixpkgs.
@malt3 Yes, we plan to back port the full vendor feature into 7.3, as 7.2 will probably be released today.
